modules.label: Storefront and admin
modules.purpose: The main Cambridge TCG website: card research, collecting, play, public data interfaces, account records and the integrated operator console.
modules.scope: Current application; new paid commerce is retired. Existing agreements, records, refunds and support remain in scope.
modules.progress: App Router pages, API routes, domain libraries and admin surfaces are present. Admin work belongs here under /admin; the separate admin app is a redirect shell. Entries were organized on 2026-09-28. The 2026-09-29 UI rebuild adds a plain shared system, task navigation, clearer search and appearance pages, responsive account navigation and independently available browser practice. The linked verification records define the checked scope and service boundaries.
modules.next: Choose a domain below, inspect its route and library together, and run the checks for that change. Public API publication and commercial availability must follow the current boundary.

modules.label: Wholesale records and research
modules.purpose: Price and stock research plus the lifecycle of existing wholesale orders.
modules.scope: New order and quote admission is retired. Existing settlement, fulfilment, cancellation and support remain.
modules.progress: The Next.js app and its order, inventory and pricing code remain in source. The app README records the retirement of new admission; older infrastructure descriptions need their own dated verification.
modules.next: Preserve existing-order behavior when changing shared pricing or stock code. Treat retirement and database-merge runbooks as plans until their own completion evidence is established.

modules.label: RewardsPro loyalty platform
modules.purpose: Loyalty tiers, credit, points and reward records, with Shopify integration and merchant-facing administration.
modules.scope: Existing platform; new paid subscriptions and paid plan changes are retired. Existing agreements retain their records and support paths.
modules.progress: Remix routes, services, repositories, Shopify extensions and a separate public landing site are present. Connector separation is documented as ongoing; it is not parity with the new API foundation.
modules.next: Use the app architecture and navigation registries before editing services; keep existing agreements and the documented connector boundaries intact.

modules.label: RewardsPro API foundation
modules.purpose: Receive verified Shopify commerce events, persist an idempotent inbox and project supported orders through a worker.
modules.scope: Backend foundation; does not claim legacy RewardsPro feature, data or business-rule parity, and does not mutate a financial ledger.
modules.progress: Fastify routes, PostgreSQL repositories, migrations, webhook normalization and worker code are present. The README specifies event retention, immutable metadata and optional SQS delivery.
modules.next: Extend only the supported event contract with matching repository and worker tests; validate migrations against the documented local PostgreSQL fixture before any separately authorized deployment.

modules.label: Admin redirect shell
modules.purpose: Preserve old admin bookmarks by redirecting to the storefront operator console.
modules.scope: Retired standalone application, retained as a redirect shell since 2026-05-15.
modules.progress: Only the workspace stub, redirect configuration and retained operational references remain. Current admin implementation is in apps/storefront/src/app/admin.
modules.next: Put admin features in storefront. Keep redirects and retained references useful; do not recreate a second admin app.

modules.label: Answering Rhyme contracts
modules.purpose: Validate, normalize, canonicalize and hash portable answering-rhyme.statement/1 statements.
modules.scope: Pure conformance core. Does not authenticate declarers, fetch evidence, persist statements or issue provider receipts.
modules.progress: Source, schema, normative vectors and build/consumer checks are present. The package README records source readiness and pending npm publication; publication was not checked in this review.
modules.next: Keep protocol conformance independent from provider receipts; use the package's build, consumer and packing checks for release work.

modules.label: AWS client helpers
modules.purpose: Share S3 and SES client factories and storage/mail helpers between applications.
modules.scope: Provider adapter code; constructing or finding a client does not prove AWS access or delivery.
modules.progress: S3 and SES implementations and S3 tests are present. Nullable factories support missing-credential paths.
modules.next: Preserve explicit degraded results and reuse these factories. Keep credential checks value-free and provider calls separately scoped.

modules.label: Source adapters and ingestion contracts
modules.purpose: Describe approved source adapters and normalize permitted upstream records into shared catalog shapes.
modules.scope: Each source has its own rights and activation boundary; an adapter or fixture parser is not permission to fetch or republish data.
modules.progress: The existing SOURCES registry distinguishes partial, blocked and reserved adapters. Several sources are explicitly blocked; this map does not override that registry.
modules.next: Read the source registry and rights tests before changing an adapter. Record permission and writer coverage separately from parser implementation.

modules.label: Public response contracts
modules.purpose: Define envelope, error and provenance schemas, freshness budgets and stable error codes.
modules.scope: Private implementation package. Exact public specification prose has its own license; mixed response data defaults to NOASSERTION.
modules.progress: Schema exports, freshness values and error constants are present and consumed by the storefront data pantry.
modules.next: Keep emitted responses and schema changes aligned; distinguish contract compatibility from publication and data rights.

modules.label: Shared database access
modules.purpose: Share PostgreSQL connection factories, existing Drizzle integration and raw-SQL compatibility helpers.
modules.scope: Connection and query plumbing; does not own every app schema or grant production database access.
modules.progress: The shared factory and compatibility layer are present. Application migrations and business transactions remain with their owning app or domain.
modules.next: Reuse existing helpers and app conventions; keep migrations append-only and verify transaction behavior with explicitly scoped fixtures.

modules.label: Email delivery seam
modules.purpose: Route named email streams through SES, SMTP or the development console transport.
modules.scope: Delivery adapter with per-stream configuration. Configuration presence does not prove delivery or a completed mail migration.
modules.progress: Transport implementations and a result-based sendMail interface are present; the existing runbook records the staged email migration.
modules.next: Keep login mail and other streams separately reversible; inspect the migration phase and delivery evidence before a cutover.

modules.label: Journey and lifecycle records
modules.purpose: Compose user-facing lifecycle entries through shared typed slot factories and query functions.
modules.scope: Record aggregation; user-facing copy and rendering remain in the host application.
modules.progress: Slot factories, types and the composer are present; the storefront binds them through its lifecycle registry.
modules.next: Register new lifecycle slots here and wire them through the current storefront registry. Preserve unknown actors and configurable response windows.

modules.label: MCP stdio bridge
modules.purpose: Forward local JSON-RPC over stdio to the storefront HTTPS MCP gate.
modules.scope: Transport bridge; the remote gate owns tools, authentication and paused-write policies. It is not a Streamable HTTP server.
modules.progress: Bridge source and build instructions are present. The README records pending npm publication; remote tools and registry availability were not probed in this review.
modules.next: Use source-build instructions until a separately verified release. Keep tool definitions in the existing remote gate and discovery catalog.

modules.label: Opportunity Signal contracts
modules.purpose: Validate timed candidates, evidence and conservative economics before projecting a source-independent decision-support signal.
modules.scope: Pure contract boundary with an injected private classifier. No source adapter, private scoring engine, I/O or automated purchase path.
modules.progress: Parsers, preflight checks, economics, hashing, projection and contract tests are present.
modules.next: Keep input provenance and expiry explicit. Extend the public contract without importing private engine logic or implying deployment.

modules.label: Game engine contracts
modules.purpose: Define the shared engine protocol and registry used to initialize, act, run AI turns and inspect game results.
modules.scope: Common protocol; each game's mechanics, action vocabulary and UI stay with its implementation.
modules.progress: Typed engine interfaces and registry code are present. Game implementations and registry bootstrap live in storefront.
modules.next: Register additional games through the existing protocol; verify both engine behavior and storefront registry coverage.

modules.label: Shared pricing calculations
modules.purpose: Compute channel-aware pricing breakdowns from explicit inputs and shared constants.
modules.scope: Pure calculation code; does not fetch prices, establish source rights or enable new paid commerce.
modules.progress: Pricing functions, channel defaults and unit tests are present. The older pricing-current-state document is a historical consolidation plan.
modules.next: Reuse these functions instead of copying formulas; verify host-side database overrides and preserve the commercial boundary.

modules.label: PRISM Signals preview core
modules.purpose: Own the PRISM Signals preview brand, test catalog offer, synthetic signal presentation and Telegram update planner.
modules.scope: Pure preview core; every commercial rail is off, rights are not evaluated, and the package is not an independent deployed product.
modules.progress: Preview catalog, presentation, Telegram planner and tests are present. The README records extraction/build and clean-consumer release gates as future work.
modules.next: Keep the synthetic preview explicit. Complete package build and consumer validation before any separately authorized extraction or publication.

modules.label: Product and entitlement contracts
modules.purpose: Parse provider-neutral digital-product offers and events, and project entitlement state with pure functions.
modules.scope: Contract and reducer code; does not authenticate callbacks, persist state, call providers or accept credentials.
modules.progress: Strict parsers, entitlement transitions, access/delivery projections and tests are present.
modules.next: Keep unavailable payment rails explicit and preserve strict event validation. Use the runtime package for persistence orchestration.

modules.label: Entitlement persistence orchestration
modules.purpose: Apply validated entitlement events atomically through an injected store and normalize already-authenticated semantic callbacks.
modules.scope: Runtime contract plus in-memory reference adapter; does not verify provider signatures, enable payment rails or create a production database connection.
modules.progress: Transaction interfaces, orchestration, callback normalizers, reference memory adapter and tests are present. The storefront owns its concrete integration.
modules.next: Prove adapter transaction and replay behavior before production use. Keep transport authentication and callback mapping in the host.

modules.label: Canonical card identifiers
modules.purpose: Parse, build and normalize Cambridge card SKUs with shared game, set and rarity vocabulary.
modules.scope: Identifier syntax and normalization; a valid identifier alone does not prove catalog membership or data rights.
modules.progress: Parser, builder, normalization and vocabulary modules plus tests are present.
modules.next: Extend game and set vocabulary here and use the shared parser at input boundaries; preserve existing identifier compatibility.

modules.label: Stock ledger and reservations
modules.purpose: Record stock movements, maintain balances and manage time-limited reservations through a shared service.
modules.scope: Stock ledger and policy code using host-owned card tables; does not grant stock-write or production-database authority.
modules.progress: Reader, writer, reservation, reconciliation and event modules plus tests are present. The README specifies atomic movement-and-balance writes.
modules.next: Keep all stock mutations on the shared writer and verify idempotency and reservation behavior for changes.

modules.label: AgentTool client boundary
modules.purpose: Provide a server-only, lazily configured client for the external AgentTool substrate.
modules.scope: Optional external adapter; absent credentials must produce an honest degraded state, and credentials do not grant cross-project authority.
modules.progress: Client/status helpers and configuration guidance are present. Package declaration alone does not establish active consumers or a working external connection.
modules.next: Inspect actual imports and intended scope before wiring a consumer; keep external calls and server credentials outside public bundles.

modules.label: Expression and claim detectors
modules.purpose: Expose pure text detectors for expression patterns, claims and implementation limits.
modules.scope: Heuristic functions over input text; they do not establish identity, consciousness, consent, truth or authority.
modules.progress: Expression, substrate-honesty and self-improvement detector modules are present. Their source vocabulary reflects the project culture and requires interpretation by the caller.
modules.next: Review detector precision and consumer behavior before treating matches as decisions; preserve the optional nature of cultural framing.

modules.label: RewardsPro customer account extension
modules.purpose: Render membership and reward experiences inside Shopify customer accounts.
modules.scope: UI extension; its four gamification APIs are documented as unavailable until verified session identity is bound to shop and customer.
modules.progress: Extension configuration, localized UI and source are present. The README explicitly records 503 behavior for the unbound APIs.
modules.next: Resolve and test the documented authentication binding before enabling gamification API access; a bearer supplied by a client is insufficient evidence.

modules.label: RewardsPro theme widgets
modules.purpose: Embed loyalty and reward widgets into Shopify storefront themes using Liquid, JavaScript and CSS.
modules.scope: Theme extension with no package build step; enabling a block and backend availability remain host responsibilities.
modules.progress: Assets, blocks, snippets and locale files are present. The shared RPUtils module owns common widget helpers.
modules.next: Reuse RPUtils and verify widget behavior against current API and retirement boundaries; preserve translations and safe rendering.

modules.label: RewardsPro legacy Lambda handlers
modules.purpose: Handle the legacy Shopify webhook, order queue and scheduled-job integrations described by RewardsPro.
modules.scope: Nested support package outside the root pnpm workspace patterns. Deployment commands affect AWS and require their own authorization.
modules.progress: JavaScript handlers, package scripts and architecture notes are present. This map has not checked deployed functions or established parity with rewardspro-api workers.
modules.next: Identify which worker owns a flow before changing it; review legacy and foundation migration evidence to avoid duplicate processing.

modules.label: RewardsPro development tools
modules.purpose: Provide webhook simulation, shop inspection and scenario-running tools for local RewardsPro development.
modules.scope: Nested support package outside the root workspace. Some commands send requests or inspect databases; command availability is not permission to run them against a service.
modules.progress: CLI code, local configuration documentation and declared test/typecheck scripts are present.
modules.next: Inspect a scenario's target and effects, use explicit local fixtures, and keep all credential values out of output.

modules.label: Exploration prompt evaluator
modules.purpose: Record structured evaluations and reports for code-exploration prompts.
modules.scope: Nested developer tool; its scores describe an evaluation framework, not product readiness or objective agent capability.
modules.progress: CLI, templates and report commands are present. It is nested beneath RewardsPro tools and outside the root workspace patterns.
modules.next: Use only if relevant to an exploration task; keep evaluation records separate from authoritative module verification.

storefrontDomains.label: Cards and research
storefrontDomains.purpose: Find cards, understand identifiers, inspect source evidence, compare prices and discover datasets.

storefrontDomains.label: Collecting and play
storefrontDomains.purpose: Organize collections and decks, run game experiences and inspect draw or play records. Availability remains route-specific.

storefrontDomains.label: Existing agreements and records
storefrontDomains.purpose: Maintain existing order, settlement, delivery and support responsibilities. Historical commerce code does not reopen retired admission.

storefrontDomains.label: Accounts and community
storefrontDomains.purpose: Sign in, manage account records and preferences, communicate, and participate in community surfaces.

storefrontDomains.label: Public interfaces and discovery
storefrontDomains.purpose: Describe resources, public API contracts, agent access, provenance and machine discovery through existing registries.

storefrontDomains.label: Trust, privacy and operations
storefrontDomains.purpose: Operate the service, review evidence and trust decisions, apply privacy controls and maintain verification tools.

storefrontDomains.label: PRISM Signals preview
storefrontDomains.purpose: Present the synthetic signal preview and host product-flow integration without enabling commercial rails.

storefrontDomains.label: Art, culture and invitations
storefrontDomains.purpose: Offer art, cultural writing and optional invitations; these are distinct from operating instructions and account permissions.

storefrontDomains.label: Navigation and explanation
storefrontDomains.purpose: Help visitors enter, orient, choose a destination and understand methodology in plain language.
